encounters.cc: Routine follow-up visit for cervical cancer surveillance

lines: Routine follow-up visit for cervical cancer surveillance
She underwent a cervical conization 18 months ago for cervical intraepithelial neoplasia 3 (CIN 3), and the surgical margins were reported to be free of disease.
She reports no abnormal vaginal bleeding, discharge, or pain.
Her last Pap smear and HPV co-testing were performed 12 months ago and were normal.
She inquires about the recommended frequency of cervical cancer screening going forward.
- History of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3
Her past medical history is significant for human papillomavirus (HPV) infection.
- Cervical conization with LEEP (18 months ago)
- Dilation and curettage for missed abortion (1 year ago)
- Vaginal delivery with midline episiotomy (6 months ago)
She has no new sexual partners and has been in a monogamous relationship for the past 5 years.
On examination, the cervix appears healthy without lesions or discharge.

encounters.cc: Six-month history of absent periods and intermittent pelvic pain

lines: Six-month history of absent periods and intermittent pelvic pain
The patient with a history of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 returns for follow-up six months after her last cervical cancer surveillance visit.
She reports that her menstrual cycles were regular until she underwent a dilation and curettage for a missed abortion one year ago.
Since the procedure, she has noticed a gradual decrease in menstrual flow and increasing dysmenorrhea.
- Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 (CIN 3), post-treatment surveillance (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- History of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3
Her past medical history is significant for a septic abortion treated with antibiotics two years ago.
- Cervical conization with LEEP (18 months ago)
- Dilation and curettage for missed abortion (1 year ago)
- Vaginal delivery with midline episiotomy (6 months ago)
On physical examination, her abdomen is soft and non-tender.
A pelvic exam reveals a normal-sized uterus with no adnexal masses or tenderness.
A hysterosalpingogram is performed and shows a filling defect in the uterine cavity with scant passage of contrast material into the proximal fallopian tubes.

encounters.cc: Severe throbbing headache beginning 48 hours after cesarean delivery

lines: Severe throbbing headache beginning 48 hours after cesarean delivery

This 33-year-old woman with a history of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 and Asherman syndrome presents to the emergency department with a severe headache that started 48 hours after she underwent a cesarean section under epidural anesthesia.
She describes the headache as throbbing, located at the front and back of her head, and notes that it significantly worsens when she stands up and improves when she lies down.
She also reports nausea and photophobia.
- Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 (CIN 3), post-treatment surveillance (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- History of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3
- Cervical conization with LEEP (18 months ago)
- Dilation and curettage for missed abortion (1 year ago)
- Vaginal delivery with midline episiotomy (6 months ago)
She has no known drug allergies
Her vital signs are within normal limits, and there is no fever
Neurological examination is normal, and there is no neck stiffness or rash.
The remainder of the physical examination is noncontributory.

encounters.cc: Severe headache and blurred vision four weeks after vaginal delivery

lines: Severe headache and blurred vision four weeks after vaginal delivery
The patient is a 34-year-old female with Asherman syndrome and prior postpartum headache who presents four weeks postpartum.
She previously presented with severe headache following cesarean delivery in 2021.
She had a normal vaginal delivery without complications and was discharged with her healthy newborn.
Her pregnancy was complicated by gestational hypertension, for which she was on labetalol until delivery.
She reports that the headache started suddenly this morning and has progressively worsened.
She denies any history of headaches like this in the past.
- Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 (CIN 3), post-treatment surveillance (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- History of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3
- Cervical conization with LEEP (18 months ago)
- Dilation and curettage for missed abortion (1 year ago)
- Vaginal delivery with midline episiotomy (6 months ago)
Physical examination reveals brisk deep tendon reflexes and 2+ lower extremity edema.
A neurological examination is significant for left-sided weakness.

encounters.cc: Difficulty controlling bowel movements six weeks after vaginal delivery

lines: Difficulty controlling bowel movements six weeks after vaginal delivery

The patient returns for six-week postpartum follow-up with a history of Asherman syndrome, cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3, and recent postpartum preeclampsia, presenting with difficulty controlling her bowel movements.
She reports unintentional passage of stool and gas, particularly when she coughs or exercises.
Her obstetric history is significant for a vaginal delivery with a midline episiotomy that extended into a third-degree laceration, which was repaired immediately post-delivery.
- Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 (CIN 3), post-treatment surveillance (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- History of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3
- Cervical conization with LEEP (18 months ago)
- Dilation and curettage for missed abortion (1 year ago)
- Vaginal delivery with midline episiotomy (6 months ago)
On physical examination, the perineal scar appears well-healed, but there is decreased anal sphincter tone and asymmetry upon contraction.
Digital rectal examination reveals a palpable defect in the external anal sphincter.

encounters.cc: Progressive pain on thumb side of wrist when lifting baby

lines: Progressive pain on thumb side of wrist when lifting baby
The patient is a 35-year-old female with history of CIN 3, Asherman syndrome, and complicated recent pregnancy.
She reports pain on the thumb side of her wrist that has been worsening over the past two weeks and is exacerbated when she lifts her 6-month-old baby.
- Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 (CIN 3), post-treatment surveillance (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- History of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3
- Cervical conization with LEEP (18 months ago)
- Dilation and curettage for missed abortion (1 year ago)
- Vaginal delivery with midline episiotomy (6 months ago)
She is not currently taking any medications
On physical examination, there is tenderness to palpation over the radial aspect of the wrist.
When performing the Finkelstein test, the patient experiences a sharp pain along the radial side of the wrist.
No erythema or edema is noted.
The patient's grip strength is normal, and there is no numbness in the hand.

encounters.cc: Persistent darkening of facial skin six months after delivery

lines: Persistent darkening of facial skin six months after delivery
This 35-year-old with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3, Asherman syndrome, and gestational diabetes presents with persistent skin changes six months postpartum.
She reports that these changes began during her second trimester of pregnancy and have persisted for 6 months postpartum.
She denies any itching or pain associated with the affected areas.
She inquires about treatment options to improve the appearance of her skin.
- Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 (CIN 3), post-treatment surveillance (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- History of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3
Her medical history is significant for gestational diabetes, which was diet-controlled and resolved after delivery.
- Cervical conization with LEEP (18 months ago)
- Dilation and curettage for missed abortion (1 year ago)
- Vaginal delivery with midline episiotomy (6 months ago)
She is currently using a moisturizer with SPF 15 when going outdoors.
On examination, you note several well-demarcated, brown, symmetrical macules on her cheeks and forehead that are more pronounced on the sun-exposed areas.
She has no other skin lesions or rashes elsewhere on her body.
The patient returns with painful intercourse in the context of CIN 3, Asherman syndrome, and recent postpartum preeclampsia and sphincter injury.
She reports that the pain is primarily at the entrance of the vagina and describes it as a burning sensation.
She gave birth to her first child 6 months ago and has been exclusively breastfeeding.
Her menstrual periods have not yet returned.
She denies any vaginal discharge or bleeding.
- Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 (CIN 3), post-treatment surveillance (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- History of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3
- Cervical conization with LEEP (18 months ago)
- Dilation and curettage for missed abortion (1 year ago)
- Vaginal delivery with midline episiotomy (6 months ago)
She is not on any medications
On physical examination, the external genitalia appear normal, but the vaginal mucosa is noted to be pale and dry, with loss of rugation.
